newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse index, futures close firmer.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse index, futures close firmer.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange swinged out from its recent doldrums on what traders attributed to fresh capital arriving to the market, pushing both the BUX index and all BUX index futures higher.
Remaining just below the 3,380.53-point all-time high, the BUX index ended at 3,375.61 points, up 36.29 points. BUX index futures closed higher for all maturities.
"The market's atmosphere was definitely positive," Peter Haas of Postabank Securities said. "There isn't anything special behind but the fact that new money came to the market."

A number of shares hit new highs amid strong demand and weak supply and traders called a positive development that investors rediscovered again meat processor Pick which jumped to above 7,000 forints to end at 7,060, up 360.
The pharma sector rode the bullish trend with both Richter and Egis hitting new highs.
Richter soared to peak at 8,200 forints, but came down to end at 8,195, up 395. Egis rose to a new high of 9,675 forints but retreated to end at 9,660, up 60.
Traders did not see any fresh fundamentals behind the strong rises but said that the new demand propels prices as the supply was weak.
Oil and gas company MOL strengthened to a daily high of 1,590 forints but later came down to end at 1,555, up 15.
"The fact that MOL will publish its first half figures tomorrow has moved investors' imagination," Haas said. "There are overheated expectations that MOL will have a strong first half," he said.

Despite that the government postponed the energy price rise to January 1, 1997 from October 1, 1996, which is expected to negatively influence MOL's annual results, investors are seen believing that strong H1 results will push its price up giving good chances for short-term speculation, traders explained.
